source.quote: When $\mu^\star \in (0,1)$, for all non-decreasing functions $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}_+$ such that $f(1) \geq 1$, the expected regret $R_T$ of the strategy of Figure~\ref{fig:Ber} is upper bounded by the infimum, as the $(c_a)_{a\in\cA}$ describe $(0,+\infty)$, of the quantities ...

source.label: th:mainBer

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Assume that $\nu^\star$ is finitely supported, with expectation $\mu^\star \in (0,1)$ and with support denoted by $\cS^\star$. Let $a \in \cA$ be a suboptimal arm such that $\mu_a > 0$ and $\nu_a$ is finitely supported. Then, for all $c_a > 0$ and all $0 < \epsilon < \min\{...\}$, the expected number of times the $\kmin$--strategy, run with $f(t)=\log t$, pulls arm $a$ satisfies ...

results.notes: Bound on expected number of pulls of a suboptimal arm (quantity other). Kinf here is defined over finitely supported distributions with mean > mu_star.

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: As a corollary, we get (by taking some common value for all $c_a$) that for all $c>0$, $\ol{R}_T \leq \sum_{a\in\cA} \Delta_a \frac{(1+c)\,\log T}{\kmin(\nu_a,\mu^\star)} + h(c)$ ... the guarantee that $\limsup_{T\rightarrow\infty} \frac{\ol{R}_T}{\log T} \leq \sum_{a\in\cA}  \frac{\Delta_a}{\kmin(\nu_a,\mu^\star)}$.

results.notes: Stated in text as corollary of Theorem 9 (not a separate numbered environment). Also implies finite-time R_T <= sum Delta_a (1+c) log T / Kinf + h(c) with h(c) unspecified constant independent of T. Arms with mu_a = 0 not explicitly treated in Theorem 9.
